spans.claim: Austin Hale was stabbed to death in the library
spans.anchor: Austin Hale lying dead in this library

spans.claim: The murder weapon was a rapier concealed in a cane
spans.anchor: bamboo cane conceals a rapier
spans.span: Who knows that this ordinary-appearing bamboo cane conceals a rapier?

spans.claim: John Hale was not at the French Embassy during the murder
spans.anchor: I was not at the French Embassy during that time
spans.span: I was not at the French Embassy during that time.

spans.anchor: Major Richards sold ten bonds of the Troy Valve Company

spans.claim: Jewelry including a Mizpah locket was stolen from Judith's bedroom
spans.anchor: theft of her jewelry to any one

spans.claim: Judith Richards wears a hidden earphone to hear
spans.anchor: the cleverly concealed earphone which she wore continually
spans.span: Judith started at the abrupt question, for Ferguson, recalling her deafness and forgetful of the cleverly concealed earphone which she wore continually, raised his voice almost to a bellow.

spans.claim: Jim Turner disguised as a maid committed theft and murder
spans.anchor: Jim Turner, disguised as a maid, murdered Austin Hale

spans.claim: Polly Davis disappeared after the murder
spans.anchor: Polly has gone

spans.claim: Robert Hale installed a dictograph in Judith's boudoir
spans.anchor: dictograph in this house
spans.span: Robert Hale, why are you using a dictograph in this house?

spans.claim: John Hale and Austin Hale had a hostile relationship
spans.anchor: you and Austin were not on good terms

spans.claim: John Hale's sword cane had bloodstains
spans.anchor: covered with blood
spans.span: One blade was covered with bloodstains.

spans.claim: Joe Richards arrived home after midnight with unexplained time gap
spans.anchor: he reached this house about twenty minutes past one
spans.span: This: according to Major Richards, he reached this house about twenty minutes past one o'clock in the morning and he was last seen in the club a little before midnight.

spans.claim: Austin Hale carried a letter in a locket
spans.anchor: carried it in a locket to have it in instant readiness
spans.span: Austin wrote me at the same time he did you, telling of the existence of such a letter, and that he carried it in a locket to have it in instant readiness.

spans.claim: Polly Davis was seen leaving the library at the time of murder
spans.anchor: she was seen leaving the library
spans.span: Polly knew he would be here Tuesday night, witness her presence in the house at midnight; she supplied him with the combination of my safe; she was seen leaving the library at the very time he must have been murdered, and his body was found lying near the _open_ safe--" "Hold on, she may have been here and all that," John broke in with rough vehemence, "but some one else may have killed Austin even in her presence--" "Then why has she not told the police?

spans.claim: The safe was found open without forced entry
spans.anchor: The lock’s not been forced
spans.span: The lock's not been forced," he muttered.

spans.claim: The stolen bonds were found in Richards' possession
spans.anchor: Joseph Richards had disposed of the ten bonds
spans.span: Joseph Richards had disposed of the ten bonds owned by his wife--which Judith desired to sell--to cover his margins in stock speculations.

spans.claim: Judith Richards was abducted and gagged to prevent her hearing
spans.anchor: blindfolded me, disconnected my earphone, and gagged me
spans.span: when some one stole behind me, blindfolded me, disconnected my earphone, and gagged me.

spans.claim: The locket contained a compromising letter
spans.anchor: a letter of a foolish, indiscreet girl
spans.span: This is a letter of a foolish, indiscreet girl, longing for a little attention, a little of this world's fun," she said soberly.

spans.anchor: You did not reach me
